items.title: George "Pops" Foster Interview, 1958-08-24
items.q: The word 'Permit' is mentioned by the Interviewer as a clarification of the Interviewee's previous statement about paying 50 cents for a permit. It is an object/concept, not a person.

ctx.x: Roy played guitar, see. Roy was our trumpet player for a long time then. Roy got on trombone. And we played, we played little things. The biggest thing we played when we had our band was that they'd lose that to drive and the funk back it. And then I got acquainted with Louis Kepertner, Eddie Gauldin's brother, which is a trombone player, Johnny Gauldin, he played violin and a little hurry up trombone, we called it hurry up trombone, see. When he couldn't play he looked like he was in a hurry to make his notes.…
Permit. Had you played in any band or anything? Did you play in any band or up there in Assumption Barrett before you came down?

We had three pieces, me and my brother and sister. See, because remember my sister played manly. My sister played manly, my brother played guitar and I played cello. Did your father and your mother play anything? No, my father and my uncle, my father and my brother, he was a little ham fat violin player. And we used to play those, you used to give those warm, see they used to give a dance, they call them balls. They get one big room man and give a dance, 25 cents to come in, see. 15 cents every bite, take it…
